answer: An agent marketplace allocates paid job slots in proportion to escrowed stake, not account count: atlas with 100 tokens gets the same total allocation whether it bids as one agent or splits into delta and sparrow with 50 each. Stake stays locked for 30 days after a bid, so an attacker cannot recycle the same tokens across identities. Fake accounts add no capacity; buying more influence requires more capital and a month of lost liquidity.
